why: The water-to-food test (reports/WATER_TO_FOOD_20261114.md) shows Egypt is capped by three global rain-fed constants applied to floodplain land: grain 1.0 t/ha, farmed share 0.6, fallow 0.6. Any floodplain rule changes harvests on every map river and belongs to the crop model; this file collects evidence for it before anything is declared or fitted.

cropping_frequency.claim: Basin (flood) irrigation permits one crop per year; multiple cropping needs perennial canals.
cropping_frequency.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica 1911, Egypt / Irrigation (citing Willcocks, Egyptian Irrigation, 2nd ed. 1899)
cropping_frequency.grade: good: standard reference, consistent with Butzer 1976

cropping_frequency.claim: Irrigated land alternately cropped and fallowed to control salinity.
cropping_frequency.source: Altaweel (Ur III salinization model, fallowing regimes as resilience strategy); a secondary Turkish article states one-year-in-two fallow
cropping_frequency.grade: weak to moderate: model study and secondary summary; Adams 1965/1981 not consulted

cultivated_share_of_floodplain.claim: About 1.75 M acres basin plus about 4 M acres perennial irrigation, i.e. about 2.33 M ha cultivated.
cultivated_share_of_floodplain.comparison: Terrain candidate area (HAND <= 5 m within 30 km of navigable rivers) is 24,554 km2 = 2.46 M ha, so cultivated land is about 0.95 of candidates in 1911.
cultivated_share_of_floodplain.grade: good for 1911; an upper bound for antiquity after a century of perennial-canal expansion

yield.claim: Public land taxed at about 8.3 artabas per aroura (Oxyrhynchite); some second-century wheat land paid rents up to 15 artabas per aroura.
yield.conversion: artaba of wheat about 30 kg; aroura 0.2756 ha; 15 artabas per aroura is about 1.6 t/ha in rent alone
yield.source: Bagnall and Worp; Rowlandson (British Academy volume)
yield.grade: moderate: read from search summaries, not the originals; bounds, not a typical yield

yield.claim: Girsu barley yields fell from about 2,537 to 897 litres per hectare between 2400 and 2100 BC.
yield.grade: unverified: do not use without the primary source

already_known_arithmetic: Applying annual cropping and a 0.95 farmed share to Egypt's water-to-food rows, and alternate-year fallow with the same farmed share to Mesopotamia, would make several Hargreaves pairs pass the declared rule and Penman-Monteith pairs fail. This was worked out informally while collecting the evidence, so any test of such a rule on these two regions is development, not validation.
needed_before_a_rule: A held-out floodplain region with water, land-use and population evidence (the Indus before 1932 lacks a qualified gauge here).
Primary sources for Mesopotamian fallow and yields (Adams 1965, 1981; Ur III texts).
A physical driver for the Egypt/Mesopotamia difference that a fantasy map can compute (flood timing against the crop, drainage or salinity), rather than region labels.
